top.title: Kepa Arrizabalaga admits Arsenal dressing room frustration after Borussia Dortmund Champions League draw despite stepping in for injured David Raya
top.description: Arsenal FC v Borussia Dortmund - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Kepa Arrizabalaga has opened up on the feeling of frustration inside the Arsenal dressing room following Tuesday's 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund. The Spanish goalkeeper was called into action at the Emirates Stadium after David Raya was sidelined with a shoulder problem. Stepping into the spotlight Arsenal maintained their unbeaten status in European competition this season, but the mood in North London was far from celebratory after a stalemate against the German giants . Kepa , who earned his first continental start of the campaign, found himself between the posts as Mikel Arteta’s side looked to solidify their position in the top eight of the league phase. The opportunity arose following a late injury blow to first-choice keeper David Raya , who sustained a shoulder issue during the weekend's Premier League clash with Newcastle United. The former Chelsea man performed well under pressure, but he admitted that the squad felt they had let two points slip away against the current Bundesliga leaders. Despite the quality of the opposition, the Gunners were the more dominant force for large periods of the contest. "We are a bit disappointed with the result," said Kepa on the club's official website . "I think it's a game that we should win, we created enough chances. I think we played very well against a very strong side. Sometimes football is like this, but if we keep playing like this, if we keep creating chances like this, I think we are in a good way." Dealing with late drama The atmosphere at the Emirates was electric as the home fans pushed for a decisive goal in the closing stages of the match. Arsenal threw everything forward in search of a winner, but the Dortmund defence held firm to secure a share of the spoils. For Kepa, the failure to find that late breakthrough was the primary source of the post-match disappointment within the camp. "We wanted the win, we were playing in front of our fans. Until the end, we pushed, the atmosphere was brilliant, I think we were very close. And when you don’t get that late goal, you are a bit frustrated, but I think we have to take the positives. I think we played very well, they are first in the Bundesliga. They are a really good team and I think we played them in a good way," the 32-year-old goalkeeper continued. Ready for the call Stepping in for Raya required a quick mental shift for Kepa, who has spent much of the season providing cover. However, the Spaniard insisted he was prepared for the challenge and was pleased to have the chance to contribute to the team’s European journey. He noted the difference between this start and other emergency appearances he has had to make in the past. top.title: C/River imposes curfew on Iso-Bendeghe, Boje over deadly land clashes
top.description: .bans entry into disputed areas, orders security agencies to enforce order By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Government has imposed an immediate dusk-to-dawn curfew on Iso-Bendeghe and Boje communities in Boki Local Government Area, following protracted clashes over a land dispute between the two neighbours. The curfew, announced Wednesday in a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Pst. Ekpenyong Cobham, will last one week from November 24, 2026. Cobham said the measure became necessary because the crisis was threatening the peace of the area. “This has become necessary as the situation has continued to threaten lives, property and peace in the area,” he said. Under the order, no movement is allowed in either community from 6 pm to 6 am daily. The statement also barred residents of both communities from entering or moving into the disputed areas “for any reason.” Security agencies were directed to enforce the curfew strictly. The government warned that violators would face the full weight of the law. “Defaulters will be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law,” the Commissioner said. The state government appealed to community leaders, youths and other stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign. It said it remained committed to ending the hostilities between the two communities. “This administration remains committed to restoring lasting peace between the two communities and appeals to leaders, youths and all stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign,” the statement said. Cobham added that the government would keep a close watch on developments in the area. “The government will continue to monitor the situation closely until normalcy returns in the area,” he said. top.title: Wolves 3-0 Derby County - fans' verdicts
top.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Tuesday's Championship match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Derby County. Here are some of your comments: Wolves fans Alan: Our best team performance of the season. Yes, we still need to be more incisive with our finishing, but apart from a spirited opening 10 minutes by Derby we were never in trouble. Mane seems to have regained his confidence and for a small, young striker showed real strength in holding off a massive Derby defender to create the first goal. Armstrong was cool in taking his two goals and Tommy Doyle was superb in midfield. Andre, Krejci and Djiga were solid at the back and Trippier and Bueno were always dangerous on the wings. Fer Lopez is all energy despite having to cope with three of four defenders. Cesar's tactics are winning the fans over, what a change from the misery of last season. Peter: Despite the scoreline, poor finishing and decision-making in and around the box held Wolves back in a game they should have won 6-0. However, Cesar is forging a formidable team, arguably having at his disposal a squad with an outstanding depth of talented players who are technically the best in the Championship. Rob: Excellent all-round performance where the dominance translated into goals for once. The defensive midfield foundation of Andre and Doyle is a revelation and Mane had an excellent game. But we need to talk about Jordan James. He was instrumental in the last two goals by pulling the Derby midfield and defence all over the place. Our strongest team would include him starting somehow. Many have intimated Lopez is carrying an injury - if that is so, James could start in his stead whilst Peixoto works on a system that could include both of them as starters. Teams will then be pushed to keep both of them quiet and I believe there would be an even more sustainable uplift in performance. December's games will be a sterner test with better opposition but Wolves can be tougher and more ruthless on this evidence. [Cody Froggatt/Press Association] Derby fans Per: We are clearly not good enough for this league. Decent defending, but we kept losing the ball and hardly created any chances. We could have scored twice (Morris and Fuseini) in the opening minutes, but we didn't take our chances and in the end we were outplayed. Philip: Absolutely awful. Route one or misplaced passes trying to play out from the back. Completely lacking in confidence. I really am not sure if Eustace can dig us out of this rut. I'd like to hope he can but I'm really not sure. Dave: Heart and fight is missing in this team. Understand the issues the proposed takeover has caused and the injuries, but our goalkeeper, who's been injured himself, is our top player too often. Need to get stuck in and get their hands dirty.

top.title: Fairfield Union’s Andy Clark is the 2025 Eagle-Gazette Coach of the Year
top.description: LANCASTER — When this year’s group of Fairfield Union football seniors were in the seventh grade, they won one game, going 1-7. Fairfield Union coach Andy Clark refused to give up on them. He believed in them and raised their standard and refused to let them fall below it. The group steadily improved and they started winning, but this season was special. The Falcons showed a lot of perseverance, stuck together when things looked bleak, and came out on the side as champions. Clark helped lead Fairfield Union to its first Mid-State League-Buckeye Division championship in 20 years. Playing Hamilton Township in a must-win situation in Week 10 to gain a share of the league title, the Falcons were able to hold on for a 14-6 victory. Fairfield Union picked up its first-ever playoff win in 2025, qualified for the playoffs again this season and hosted a first-round game. The Falcons finished with a 6-1 league mark and went 8-3 overall. Because of his leadership, Clark is the 2026 Eagle-Gazette Football Coach of the Year. More: Fairfield Union clinches a share of the Mid-State League-Buckeye title He was thankful for the recognition but wanted to talk more about what the team accomplished and how their hard work enabled them to achieve what they did. “Football is the most team-oriented sport on planet Earth, so anytime individual awards are given out, it’s clearly a group effort,” Clark said. “You have to have players that have bought in. They set goals, and they worked to achieve those. For that to happen, a lot of good things had to be in place, and that’s what makes it the most rewarding.” What made it even more special for Clark was how far the team had come, especially the seniors. “It was a group that could have given up on themselves and each other, but they stuck together,” Clark said. “They continued to work hard, they pushed each other, and they have a tight bond. They shared in all that pain and disappointment when they were younger, and even early in their high school careers. They really worked their tails off and made improvements each year, and it led to this year. They were playing big games at the end of the season, and I don’t know without that tough beginning they would be where they are now. They dealt with a lot of adversity in their careers. It’s just a testament to them sticking together.” The fact that the Falcons were able to hang on and pull out such a huge victory over the Rangers in the last game of the regular season, with so much on the line, it all went back to Clark holding his team to a higher standard and the belief they could win big games. “They were so prepared for that game, and they were locked in,” Clark said. “It was just neat to see it all come together. I was happy for them to see how far they had come to get to that moment with so much on the line. It was so gratifying to see them celebrate after that game. It all went back to holding them to the standard that it takes to achieve the goals they wanted to achieve.

Clark had an outstanding season as he led the Falcons to an 8-3 overall record. He accounted for 1,888 total yards and 21 touchdowns. People seldom feel sorry for Alabama, or any SEC school for that matter, but Crimson Tide basketball head coach Nate Oats is more convinced than ever that his program was wrongfully criticized for putting former G League player Charles Bediako on the roster last season. He takes serious issue with the villain narrative that swirled around Tuscaloosa, especially since eligibility controversy is quite commonplace now. Oats was already not in a great mood following his team’s 68-63 Players Era 16 loss versus Baylor, so what better way to blow off steam than by dwelling on the past and taking shots at his contemporaries . “A lot of those coaches wanted to speak on the Bediako thing, well, they’re doing the exact thing this year,” the two-time SEC champion said from Las Vegas, Nevada’s T-Mobile Arena, per BamaCentral’s Theodore Fernandez. “Yeah, it does bother me. The former SEC Coach of the Year believes he was unfairly condemned for taking advantage of the system, particularly because others are now following his lead. That being said, he may be forgetting just how unusual the Bediako situation was. The Canadian big man returned to Alabama last season after being out of college for almost three years. Despite a fairly blatant circumvention of collegiate athletic ethics, Alabama was not in danger of being ousted from the conference. LSU is not a victim, either, to be clear, but this notion that the Crimson Tide were mercilessly ripped apart ignores certain context. top.title: CAF releases finalists for 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award (Full list)
top.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has released the five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi, Senegal’s Sadio Mané and three other players making the shortlist. The final nominees were selected from an initial list of 10 players based on their performances for club and country during the period under consideration. Morocco has three representatives on the list, while Senegal has two, reflecting the countries’ strong performances in the period. Hakimi, who plays for French champions Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the award after helping the club win the UEFA Champions League and French Ligue 1 title. The Moroccan defender also captained his national team during its campaigns at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is also in contention for a third title after helping Senegal win the 2025 AFCON. The Al-Nassr forward was named the tournament’s Best Player in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Senegal’s triumph. Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz earned a place on the shortlist following his performances for Morocco, particularly at the 2025 AFCON, where he won the Golden Boot with five goals. Villarreal midfielder Pape Gueye also made the list after scoring the winning goal in extra time as Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the AFCON final in Rabat. His performances at the tournament also earned him a place in the Best XI. Completing the shortlist is Morocco’s Ismael Saibari, who played an important role in his country’s run to the AFCON final, including scoring against Cameroon in the quarter-finals. The winner will be announced at the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos. The ceremony is expected to begin at 7pm Nigerian time. The CAF Awards will return to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition. top.title: Meta unveils $700,000 AI grant for Nigerian startups
top.description: By Juliet Umeh Meta has announced a $700,000 artificial intelligence (AI) grant programme for startups and developers in Nigeria and six other countries, as part of efforts to accelerate AI innovation and expand access to emerging technologies. The programme, scheduled to commence in 2027, will cover Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), according to a statement issued by the company on Tuesday. Meta said the grant would support startups and developers building solutions using its AI tools and wearable technologies. The company also announced the launch of a new hub designed to provide educational resources and information on its AI developments, partnerships and innovation initiatives across Africa, the Middle East and Turkey. The hub will operate through three learning programmes: AI Academy, AI Literacy and AI for Small and Medium-sized Businesses. The programmes are designed for students, developers, entrepreneurs and business professionals, with Meta targeting more than five million beneficiaries across the three regions over the next three years. Meta’s Vice-President of Public Policy for Africa, the Middle East and Turkey, Kojo Boakye, said the initiatives were designed to equip developers and entrepreneurs with the skills, resources and support needed to build AI solutions that address challenges in their communities. “AI’s value will be judged by the real impact it has on people’s lives,” Boakye said. “Across our region, people are building solutions around the languages they speak, the businesses they run and the challenges their communities face. “The Impact Grant and Hub are about giving more builders the support, skills and resources to turn those ideas into useful products and services. We want people here to help shape AI’s future, not simply use what others have built.” In another initiative, Meta announced the AMET AI Awards 2026, with more than $100,000 in prizes across seven categories to recognise outstanding AI innovations. The company said the awards would recognise finalists from its AI Academy and Wearables Studio programmes, including students, developers and startups. The award categories include Wearables Innovation of the Year, AI Builder of the Year, Emerging Innovator of the Year and Startup of the Year. Others are AI for Accessibility and Inclusion, AI for Social and Economic Impact, and People’s Choice, which will be decided through a live vote by attendees at the summit. Meta said the awards would recognise projects leveraging AI-powered technologies to address everyday needs, improve access to opportunities and services, and promote social and economic development. top.title: Opel and Citroen exit is not a betrayal of Formula E, but a major blow at the worst possible time
top.description: Motorsport photo What many had feared has unfortunately come to pass. In light of the substantial financial hole that emerged at the end of 2025 and the losses recorded in the third quarter of this year, Stellantis has decided to close almost all of its programmes, including those in Formula E, which at the end of 2027 will lose Citroen and Opel. However, it is important to understand that this decision goes beyond a single category and is not a barometer of the championship's health. This is not a betrayal of Formula E, of what it represents or its value, as the simultaneous departure from the WEC with Peugeot shows. Rather, it is a reflection of the very complex moment the entire European automotive sector is going through. Read Also: Peugeot quits WEC, Citroen and Opel to wind down Formula E programmes Stellantis has not yet reported its full financial results for 2026, with the latest statement currently stopping at the third-quarter losses, but the company's senior management has repeatedly said that in 2027 the rising price of raw materials could cost not millions, but billions. The exit from racing programmes starts here: the problem is not motorsport, but what lies upstream. On the contrary, Formula E was conceived as a financially sustainable category, precisely to attract the major manufacturers. It is a model that worked for years, to the point that today there is no shortage of leading brands. However, for a series whose main strength is in manufacturers' commitment, losing two brands in one go is the equivalent of a well-placed right hook. It is easy to understand why sporting projects are the first to be cut in difficult times, but both Opel and Citroen have already invested a significant part of the budget allocated to the 2027 season, so much so that they will contest the season. top.title: Taylor Lewan thinks Caleb Williams could do what no NFL player has ever done before
top.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images Caleb Williams is only in the midst of his third season in the NFL but he is already being touted to achieve big things. The young quarterback suffered a hamstring strain back in September but has since shone upon his return to help the Chicago Bears go 8-2. Amid his impressive form, Taylor Lewan has now floated the idea that Williams could be named the NFL MVP and win the Comeback Player of the Year award in 2026. Speaking via a podcast this week, he said: “Caleb Williams, though. Tell you what, stud. MVP-calibre guy. Comeback Player of the Year in the same year.” One of his fellow hosts then pointed out: “Yep. That would be the first time ever,” to which Lewan responded: “That would be unbelievable. He’s a phenomenal quarterback and talent.” How Caleb Williams compares to other MVP candidates Because of his injury, Williams has only played seven games so far this season. So, it is hard to judge him on overall stats like passing yards, which he ranks 25th in the league for with 1,727, and passing touchdowns, which he ranks 19th for (10) When it comes to per game stats, the Bears ace has a 68.3% completion rate, which is the eighth-highest in the NFL and below several MVP candidates like Joe Burrow (74.2%) and Brock Purdy (71.0%). Elsewhere, he is throwing for 246.7 yards per game. That is the 11th-highest total in the league but again, still off the pace of big names like Purdy (262.4), Burrow (309.5), Patrick Mahomes (270.9) and Jordan Love (283.8). Williams’ average yards per pass attempt isn’t that amazing either. His 7.9 average (10th overall) puts him below Lamar Jackson (10.0), Purdy (9.0), Trevor Lawrence (8.4), Josh Allen (8.4), Burrow (8.1) and more. So, while he is having a good season and should have plenty of years ahead of him in the NFL to keep getting better, he doesn’t really look to be on the same level as other top quarterbacks just yet. The decision removes the immediate sporting consequence for Mauricio Pochettino’s side, but it has not brought full agreement on the incident itself. Yoro was sent off inside the opening eight minutes of United’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool after colliding with Alexander Isak as the forward broke through on goal. The dismissal proved a major turning point in a one-sided contest, with Liverpool taking full control and United unable to recover after going down to 10 men. It also spares Yoro, one of the club’s key young defenders, from further disruption after a difficult afternoon at Anfield. top.title: After further review, Kent State football win turns into a loss
top.description: YPSILANTI, MICH. — Upon further review, Kent State's 2026 college football season ended in the most brutal way possible. Ethan Thanthanavong's winning 14-yard touchdown pass to Wayne Harris on fourth down with one second left was overturned, and the Golden Flashes left Rynearson Stadium with a 17-12 loss to Eastern Michigan on Nov. 24. A television replay showed Harris getting one foot inbounds as he caught the ball in the back of the end zone. He appeared to have possession as he landed. After a replay review, the officials determined that Harris did not have possession. The Flashes finished the season at 3-9 overall and 2-6 in the Mid-American Conference. The overturned call cost Harris an opportunity to become only the fourth 1,000-yard receiver in program history. He caught five passes for 125 yards and finished the season with 60 catches for 988 yards. Brendyn Smith scored Kent State's two touchdowns. He caught a 17-yard touchdown pass from Thanthanavong and returned a kickoff 100 yards for a TD. top.title: Musiala first examined due to absence-like symptoms after new contract
top.description: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala sits on the bench prior to the start of the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and 1. FC Cologne at Allianz Arena. "As there have been many rumours in recent days, FC Bayern and 11WINS, the agency representing Jamal, wish to clarify: Jamal Musiala was first examined on 22 April 2025 due to absence-like symptoms," the club said in a statement on Wednesday. "This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared." Musiala signed a contract extension until June 2030 in February 2025. The player's health condition and contract situation have been under the spotlight in recent weeks after public remarks from club officials. After collapsing twice during pre-season, Musiala said he has been affected by absence seizures, a form of epilepsy, and has missed some of the campaign because of it. He has struggled for his best form when he has played. Honorary president Uli Hoeness spoke of a dilemma for the club, while chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen raised the prospect of talks with Musiala's management and family. Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge also questioned the 23-year-old's lucrative contract signed just last year if he does not hit the same heights as earlier in his career. Doctors have said there is no reason his form should suffer. Bayern had a meeting with Musiala's management on Tuesday and the club spoke of constructive talks. "A constructive meeting took place between FC Bayern Munich and the management of Jamal Musiala yesterday (Tuesday). For both sides, the player's health comes above everything else. nigeria.title: C/River imposes curfew on Iso-Bendeghe, Boje over deadly land clashes
nigeria.description: .bans entry into disputed areas, orders security agencies to enforce order By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Government has imposed an immediate dusk-to-dawn curfew on Iso-Bendeghe and Boje communities in Boki Local Government Area, following protracted clashes over a land dispute between the two neighbours. The curfew, announced Wednesday in a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Pst. Ekpenyong Cobham, will last one week from November 24, 2026. Cobham said the measure became necessary because the crisis was threatening the peace of the area. “This has become necessary as the situation has continued to threaten lives, property and peace in the area,” he said. Under the order, no movement is allowed in either community from 6 pm to 6 am daily. The statement also barred residents of both communities from entering or moving into the disputed areas “for any reason.” Security agencies were directed to enforce the curfew strictly. The government warned that violators would face the full weight of the law. “Defaulters will be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law,” the Commissioner said. The state government appealed to community leaders, youths and other stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign. It said it remained committed to ending the hostilities between the two communities. “This administration remains committed to restoring lasting peace between the two communities and appeals to leaders, youths and all stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign,” the statement said. Cobham added that the government would keep a close watch on developments in the area. “The government will continue to monitor the situation closely until normalcy returns in the area,” he said. nigeria.title: CAF releases finalists for 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award (Full list)
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has released the five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi, Senegal’s Sadio Mané and three other players making the shortlist. The final nominees were selected from an initial list of 10 players based on their performances for club and country during the period under consideration. Morocco has three representatives on the list, while Senegal has two, reflecting the countries’ strong performances in the period. Hakimi, who plays for French champions Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the award after helping the club win the UEFA Champions League and French Ligue 1 title. The Moroccan defender also captained his national team during its campaigns at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is also in contention for a third title after helping Senegal win the 2025 AFCON. The Al-Nassr forward was named the tournament’s Best Player in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Senegal’s triumph. Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz earned a place on the shortlist following his performances for Morocco, particularly at the 2025 AFCON, where he won the Golden Boot with five goals. Villarreal midfielder Pape Gueye also made the list after scoring the winning goal in extra time as Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the AFCON final in Rabat. His performances at the tournament also earned him a place in the Best XI. Completing the shortlist is Morocco’s Ismael Saibari, who played an important role in his country’s run to the AFCON final, including scoring against Cameroon in the quarter-finals. The winner will be announced at the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos. The ceremony is expected to begin at 7pm Nigerian time. The CAF Awards will return to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition. nigeria.title: Meta unveils $700,000 AI grant for Nigerian startups
nigeria.description: By Juliet Umeh Meta has announced a $700,000 artificial intelligence (AI) grant programme for startups and developers in Nigeria and six other countries, as part of efforts to accelerate AI innovation and expand access to emerging technologies. The programme, scheduled to commence in 2027, will cover Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), according to a statement issued by the company on Tuesday. Meta said the grant would support startups and developers building solutions using its AI tools and wearable technologies. The company also announced the launch of a new hub designed to provide educational resources and information on its AI developments, partnerships and innovation initiatives across Africa, the Middle East and Turkey. The hub will operate through three learning programmes: AI Academy, AI Literacy and AI for Small and Medium-sized Businesses. The programmes are designed for students, developers, entrepreneurs and business professionals, with Meta targeting more than five million beneficiaries across the three regions over the next three years. Meta’s Vice-President of Public Policy for Africa, the Middle East and Turkey, Kojo Boakye, said the initiatives were designed to equip developers and entrepreneurs with the skills, resources and support needed to build AI solutions that address challenges in their communities. “AI’s value will be judged by the real impact it has on people’s lives,” Boakye said. “Across our region, people are building solutions around the languages they speak, the businesses they run and the challenges their communities face. “The Impact Grant and Hub are about giving more builders the support, skills and resources to turn those ideas into useful products and services. We want people here to help shape AI’s future, not simply use what others have built.” In another initiative, Meta announced the AMET AI Awards 2026, with more than $100,000 in prizes across seven categories to recognise outstanding AI innovations. The company said the awards would recognise finalists from its AI Academy and Wearables Studio programmes, including students, developers and startups. The award categories include Wearables Innovation of the Year, AI Builder of the Year, Emerging Innovator of the Year and Startup of the Year. Others are AI for Accessibility and Inclusion, AI for Social and Economic Impact, and People’s Choice, which will be decided through a live vote by attendees at the summit. Meta said the awards would recognise projects leveraging AI-powered technologies to address everyday needs, improve access to opportunities and services, and promote social and economic development. nigeria.title: Zamfara: Bandits kill two headmasters, 13 others, abduct residents
nigeria.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Armed bandits have killed 15 people, including two primary school headmasters and an 11-month-old baby, in separate attacks on communities in Zamfara State. The attacks, which occurred in Tungan Janbuzu and Madanbaji communities, also left several residents abducted, according to a report by the BBC Hausa Service. The two headmasters, identified as Kabiru Salisu and Shehu Umar, both aged 35, were reportedly killed in an ambush at Janbuzu. A resident of the community, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 4pm, following the escape of some kidnapped residents from their captors. He explained that the bandits had earlier abducted some locals from Janbuzu and kept them in captivity, forcing them to work for their captors. According to him, the kidnappers had demanded a ransom of N300,000, which was subsequently delivered to them at a location near Kiawa. He said the bandits collected the money but later drove the person who delivered it away, claiming that the payment was meant for recharge cards and fuel. The resident further narrated that the bandits had taken six captives into the bush, tied them up and left them under the supervision of a young boy while they went to Aboro to purchase drugs and other supplies. However, the captives reportedly managed to untie themselves, overpower their guard, seize his gun and escape after beating him. The resident said the escape angered other members of the gang, who were reportedly hiding on a nearby farm. He said the armed men subsequently ambushed the two headmasters near a location known as Gora, seized their mobile phones and shot them dead. The resident, however, said kidnapping incidents had reduced considerably in the area, except in communities located close to the forests and bushes where the bandits operate. He expressed concern over the continued vulnerability of residents in remote settlements, despite the reported reduction in kidnapping incidents. Morka said anyone accused of rigging an election should be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law, rather than subjected to punishment determined by political parties or their supporters. His comments followed remarks by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, who had defended the slogan during an interview with Channels Television after the party’s town hall meeting in Taraba State on Tuesday. nigeria.description: …Banks to receive dollar cash from apex bank to meet demand By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has temporarily raised the weekly dollar cash purchase limit for Bureau De Change (BDC) operators from $150,000 to $1 million, as part of measures to address seasonal demand pressures in the foreign exchange market. The apex bank also pledged to supply authorised dealer banks with dollar cash to meet the requirements of their BDC customers, allowing licensed operators to access up to 100 per cent of their foreign exchange purchases in cash. The development was confirmed by bankers and forex dealers who spoke to Vanguard, following an email communication from the CBN on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, outlining the new operational arrangements. Kunle Ezun, Chief Economist, Ecobank Nigeria, confirmed the development, saying: “Very correct. The message was sent yesterday. The banks are putting machinery in place to commence the sale. It will be T+2.” Taiwo Ebenezer, Chairman, Association of Bureaux De Change Operators of Nigeria (ABCON), South-West Zone, also confirmed the directive, saying some banks had already contacted BDC operators. “Yes sir, some banks have been calling. CBN also promised to fund the banks,” he said. In an email dated November 24, 2026, sent by Yasir Shanono Shehu and Aderinola Shonekan, of the CBN, the apex bank said the measures were designed “to address seasonal demand pressures and improve orderly access to US$ cash for end users.” The apex bank stated: “All licensed BDCs (please see attached) may access US$ cash for FX purchased at the NFEM through the Authorised Dealer Banks (ADBs) with which they hold accounts, and the CBN will support ADBs with any cash requirements to meet the demand of their BDC clients.” Under the new arrangement, “the approved licensed BDCs may receive up to 100% of an approved FX purchase in US$ cash from the ADB where they hold their settlement account.” The CBN added that “the weekly purchase cap is temporarily increased from USD 150,000 to a maximum of USD 1 million per BDC.” BDCs are required to submit requests through the BDC FX Purchase Tracker (FXBT), while authorised dealer banks are expected to acknowledge requests same day and confirm or reject them on the portal, stating reasons for any rejection. According to the CBN, “ADBs shall consolidate confirmed cash requirements, which will be validated against the FXBT, after which the CBN will supply US$ cash to the ADBs for onward disbursement to the BDCs.” On settlement, the apex bank said: “Settlement between the CBN, ADBs and BDCs is on a T+2 basis, i.e. two (2) business days after the trade date on which the ADB confirms the request on the FXBT. The BDC’s settlement account shall be debited at the point of cash disbursement.” The CBN, however, said existing documentation and KYC/CDD requirements, the prohibition of third-party transactions and the 24-hour sell-back rule remain in force and apply equally to cash transactions. nigeria.title: ‘Ebube Dike’: Tinubu pays tribute to late Nollywood legend Pete Edochie
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab President Bola Tinubu has mourned veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie, describing his death as a great loss to Nigeria and the film industry. Tinubu said Edochie was one of the progenitors of Nigeria’s vibrant film industry and an exceptional actor whose contributions to African storytelling would remain memorable for generations. The President, while stating this in a tribute shared on the official X account of his Special Adviser Information and Strategy, recalled the late actor’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s novel, Things Fall Apart , in the 1980s. Describing the actor as one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians, Tinubu said, “Chief Edochie was an exceptional actor – one of the progenitors of our vibrant film industry, Nollywood. He was graceful and larger than life, both on the screen and in person. “He was one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians. For decades, he plied his craft, bringing joy, laughter, and charm to many homes.” The President also recalled Edochie’s performances in productions such as Igodo , Rituals and Lionheart , noting that they helped shape the evolution and international visibility of Nollywood. According to him, the actor’s portrayal of traditional institutions, family structures, African values and human relationships helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences worldwide. Tinubu further highlighted Edochie’s contributions beyond acting, describing him as an administrator, broadcaster and journalist. “Pete Edochie was not only an actor; he was also an administrator, broadcaster, and journalist – truly one of our finest. His place in the pantheon of those who shaped the film industry, our common norms, and popular culture remains indisputable,” he said. Reflecting on the actor’s legacy, the President said Edochie had lived a fulfilled life and would continue to be remembered through his body of work. “Pete Edochie lived well. He played his part and exited gracefully. “In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather,” Tinubu added. The President extended his condolences to the Edochie family, friends, associates and the Nigerian film industry on behalf of his family and the Federal Government. He concluded his tribute with a prayer for the late actor, saying, “May God Almighty grant ‘Ebube Dike’ eternal rest.” The post ‘Ebube Dike’: Tinubu pays tribute to late Nollywood legend Pete Edochie appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Tashima vows to serve single term if he wins FIFA election
nigeria.description: FIFA presidential candidate Kozo Tashima said Wednesday that he planned to serve only one term of four years if he beats Gianni Infantino and Philippe Diallo in March’s election. Japan’s Tashima has pledged to restore “integrity” to world football’s governing body and is one of three names on the ballot along with current president Infantino and French football chief Diallo. Infantino has faced stinging criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup but he retains considerable support for his bid for a fourth and final term. Tashima admits that he has only an outside chance of winning but pledged to make his time in charge brief if he is elected. “I am currently putting together a manifesto but basically I plan to serve for one term of four years,” the 69-year-old told reporters in Tokyo. “In those four years I plan to focus on changing governance at FIFA. I believe we have to make the processes within FIFA more transparent.” Tashima said last week that he was not “at this point” thinking of dropping out of the race in order to give Diallo a straight fight against Infantino. Diallo has Europe’s backing and is seen as the likelier candidate to unseat the current president. Tashima said he had spoken to Diallo by phone and intends to meet him in person in Europe. He said they were both “heading in the same direction” and would consult over tactics. “As we go forward, if we continue to communicate we may find our direction does indeed align or we may find we have some differences,” he said. “The main goal is to bring FIFA back onto the right track, and we are looking at various options to achieve that.” The post Tashima vows to serve single term if he wins FIFA election appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Malaysia Sues Google For $146m Over YouTube Content
nigeria.description: Malaysia said Wednesday it was suing Google for $146 million over the tech giant’s failure to remove “harmful” content posted on video-sharing platform YouTube. “The lawsuits concern two separate matters involving Google’s alleged failure to comply with its statutory obligations and applicable licence conditions,” the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission said. The first suit related to the US firm’s alleged failure to take action against “thousands of online materials including gambling, scams and fraud”, the watchdog said in a statement. The MCMC said it had submitted 73,703 reports to YouTube between January 1 and October 28 this year, the majority of which related to online gambling. In this file photo taken on June 28, 2013 a webcam is positioned in front of YouTube’s logo in Paris. (Photo by LIONEL BONAVENTURE / AFP) Of these gambling-related reports, some 4,950 cases received no response, while a further 35 cases took more than 90 days for a platform response or takedown, the MCMC added. A further 1,468 cases exceeded 30 days from the date of submission, it added. “These figures demonstrate the scale of harmful content on the platform and the delays in addressing such content,” the watchdog said. The second case related to YouTube’s failure to take down alleged defamatory and false content posted by a Malaysian blogger after the MCMC received a complaint. Google could not immediately be reached for comment. The lawsuits came three weeks after Google announced plans to invest $15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure, expanding on a $2 billion investment announced in 2024. The country is Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing hub for new data centres crammed with servers that can train and run AI tools such as chatbots and image generators. Malaysia had previously taken other major social media platforms, including TikTok, to task over allegations that they had failed to remove content deemed “grossly offensive”. nigeria.title: Trump hails Infantino as USA to co-host 2031 Women’s World Cup
nigeria.description: President Donald Trump praised embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday while celebrating the United States being named a co-host of the 2031 Women’s World Cup. Infantino, who gave Trump the first FIFA Peace Prize last December, is fighting to keep his job after causing outrage in July with a shortlived plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. A FIFA election next March in Morocco will decide if Infantino keeps his job against rival contenders Philippe Diallo of France and Kozo Tashima of Japan. “Thank you to Gianni Infantino, and his great staff, for working to bring the Tournament to the USA,” Trump posted on social media. Trump and Infantino awarded Spain the trophy at this year’s final of the World Cup, which was co-hosted by Canada and Mexico. FIFA confirmed Monday that the United States will co-host the 2031 Women’s World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after Infantino noted it was the “sole candidacy” for the tournament. “I am proud to announce that the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will take place in the United States!” Trump posted. “After hosting the Most Successful World Cup in History, no Country is better positioned than the United States to be home to the largest Women’s Sporting Event in History.” The Women’s World Cup field will expand to a record 48 teams in 2031. “The FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will bring Generational Economic Impact to the United States, grow the sport of Soccer throughout our Country and the World, and showcase America’s Exceptionalism,” Trump posted. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: How Williams Alamu Graduated with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan
entertainment.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. The thought of getting a B or C frightened me so much that I eventually decided not to sit for the examinations. entertainment.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. I have probably said that last part a hundred times since getting my results, and honestly, I don’t think I’m tired of saying it yet. Haha! One thing about me is that I like to be involved. entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? sports.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Tuesday's Championship match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Derby County. Here are some of your comments: Wolves fans Alan: Our best team performance of the season. Yes, we still need to be more incisive with our finishing, but apart from a spirited opening 10 minutes by Derby we were never in trouble. Mane seems to have regained his confidence and for a small, young striker showed real strength in holding off a massive Derby defender to create the first goal. Armstrong was cool in taking his two goals and Tommy Doyle was superb in midfield. Andre, Krejci and Djiga were solid at the back and Trippier and Bueno were always dangerous on the wings. Fer Lopez is all energy despite having to cope with three of four defenders. Cesar's tactics are winning the fans over, what a change from the misery of last season. Peter: Despite the scoreline, poor finishing and decision-making in and around the box held Wolves back in a game they should have won 6-0. Rob: Excellent all-round performance where the dominance translated into goals for once. The defensive midfield foundation of Andre and Doyle is a revelation and Mane had an excellent game. But we need to talk about Jordan James. He was instrumental in the last two goals by pulling the Derby midfield and defence all over the place. Our strongest team would include him starting somehow. sports.description: LANCASTER — When this year’s group of Fairfield Union football seniors were in the seventh grade, they won one game, going 1-7. Fairfield Union coach Andy Clark refused to give up on them. He believed in them and raised their standard and refused to let them fall below it. The group steadily improved and they started winning, but this season was special. The Falcons showed a lot of perseverance, stuck together when things looked bleak, and came out on the side as champions. Clark helped lead Fairfield Union to its first Mid-State League-Buckeye Division championship in 20 years. Playing Hamilton Township in a must-win situation in Week 10 to gain a share of the league title, the Falcons were able to hold on for a 14-6 victory. Fairfield Union picked up its first-ever playoff win in 2025, qualified for the playoffs again this season and hosted a first-round game. The Falcons finished with a 6-1 league mark and went 8-3 overall. Because of his leadership, Clark is the 2026 Eagle-Gazette Football Coach of the Year. More: Fairfield Union clinches a share of the Mid-State League-Buckeye title He was thankful for the recognition but wanted to talk more about what the team accomplished and how their hard work enabled them to achieve what they did. “Football is the most team-oriented sport on planet Earth, so anytime individual awards are given out, it’s clearly a group effort,” Clark said. “You have to have players that have bought in. They set goals, and they worked to achieve those. For that to happen, a lot of good things had to be in place, and that’s what makes it the most rewarding.” What made it even more special for Clark was how far the team had come, especially the seniors. “It was a group that could have given up on themselves and each other, but they stuck together,” Clark said. “They continued to work hard, they pushed each other, and they have a tight bond. They shared in all that pain and disappointment when they were younger, and even early in their high school careers. They really worked their tails off and made improvements each year, and it led to this year. They were playing big games at the end of the season, and I don’t know without that tough beginning they would be where they are now. They dealt with a lot of adversity in their careers. It’s just a testament to them sticking together.” The fact that the Falcons were able to hang on and pull out such a huge victory over the Rangers in the last game of the regular season, with so much on the line, it all went back to Clark holding his team to a higher standard and the belief they could win big games. “They were so prepared for that game, and they were locked in,” Clark said. “It was just neat to see it all come together. I was happy for them to see how far they had come to get to that moment with so much on the line. It was so gratifying to see them celebrate after that game. It all went back to holding them to the standard that it takes to achieve the goals they wanted to achieve.

sports.title: Taylor Lewan thinks Caleb Williams could do what no NFL player has ever done before
sports.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images Caleb Williams is only in the midst of his third season in the NFL but he is already being touted to achieve big things. The young quarterback suffered a hamstring strain back in September but has since shone upon his return to help the Chicago Bears go 8-2. Amid his impressive form, Taylor Lewan has now floated the idea that Williams could be named the NFL MVP and win the Comeback Player of the Year award in 2026. Speaking via a podcast this week, he said: “Caleb Williams, though. Tell you what, stud. MVP-calibre guy. Comeback Player of the Year in the same year.” One of his fellow hosts then pointed out: “Yep. That would be the first time ever,” to which Lewan responded: “That would be unbelievable. He’s a phenomenal quarterback and talent.” How Caleb Williams compares to other MVP candidates Because of his injury, Williams has only played seven games so far this season. So, it is hard to judge him on overall stats like passing yards, which he ranks 25th in the league for with 1,727, and passing touchdowns, which he ranks 19th for (10) When it comes to per game stats, the Bears ace has a 68.3% completion rate, which is the eighth-highest in the NFL and below several MVP candidates like Joe Burrow (74.2%) and Brock Purdy (71.0%). Elsewhere, he is throwing for 246.7 yards per game. That is the 11th-highest total in the league but again, still off the pace of big names like Purdy (262.4), Burrow (309.5), Patrick Mahomes (270.9) and Jordan Love (283.8). Williams’ average yards per pass attempt isn’t that amazing either. His 7.9 average (10th overall) puts him below Lamar Jackson (10.0), Purdy (9.0), Trevor Lawrence (8.4), Josh Allen (8.4), Burrow (8.1) and more. So, while he is having a good season and should have plenty of years ahead of him in the NFL to keep getting better, he doesn’t really look to be on the same level as other top quarterbacks just yet. sports.title: Marshall Faulk shared his Parkinson's diagnosis for one selfless reason | Opinion
sports.description: BATON ROUGE, La. – Eric Dickerson warned him. After Marshall Faulk hung up his spikes following an amazing 12-year career as one of the greatest running backs in NFL history, Dickerson told him what to expect as a former football player in retirement. Those old football injuries, Dickerson cautioned, never really go away. “Eric warned me,” Faulk, 53, told USA TODAY Sports during a wide-ranging interview in his office at Southern University , where he is winding down his first season as a rookie head coach. "Like when I retired, I think I was 33, he said, 'When you get to be 43 or 48, check back with me then.'" It brought back the memory of a conversation I had a few years ago with Dickerson, himself one of the greatest running backs ever, when he mentioned how difficult it was for him to get a good night’s sleep. He told me about nagging aches from various injuries – including from a shot he took in the chest from a late hit after scoring a touchdown decades ago – that sometimes popped up from nowhere. When I told Faulk about my chat with his fellow Hall of Famer, he grinned and nodded. “That is so true,” Faulk said. “I think at 48, I tore my Achilles. I was like, ‘Damn!’ ” What were you doing? “Nothing, man, nothing. Seriously.” You weren’t on the golf course? “Nothing. Literally, I took a step down. Pop. Nothing,” Faulk described. MORE JARRETT BELL: Forget Parkinson's. Marshall Faulk is building a football power at Southern | Exclusive Why Marshall Faulk revealed Parkinson's diagnosis The foot has long been fully healed, yet Faulk has gone public with his current health challenge. He recently revealed that he was diagnosed about a year-and-half ago with the early stages of Parkinson’s disease. He’s so upbeat about his prospects for managing this – which includes medication – and that he has had no progressive symptoms. According to experts, Parkinson’s is considered a risk factor, but not a direct cause, for neurological decline. Still, it may be natural to wonder – on the heels of former All-Pro running back Chris Johnson’s disclosure in July that he is battling ALS , which has robbed him of his ability to speak and left him bound to a wheelchair; and with former running back Roger Craig using his Hall of Fame induction speech in August to announce that he has been dealing with vascular dementia – whether Faulk’s Parkinson’s diagnosis is linked to football. The same shocks to the body absorbed in football that can blow out knees and dislocate ankles, for example, can also rattle brains. Faulk’s discovery began on the golf course, when stiffness in joints prompted him to seek evaluation. “You know, I have some stiffness in my wrist, my hand, my elbow,” he said. “At times, it would just freeze up. I thought, ‘Hey, that’s par for the course. I played professional football.’ And then to find out it’s something else, it’s like, ‘OK, yeah.’ ” Marshall Faulk NFL career stats Faulk was 33 when he played his final season with the St. Louis Rams in 2005

sports.title: ‘Let them learn’ – Why Peyton Manning is desperate for young QBs to break his rookie record
sports.description: Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images Peyton Manning had a historic rookie year filled with record-setting numbers, but the Broncos and Colts legend is ready to pass the mantle on to a new young quarterback. Manning’s 1998 rookie season was phenomenal, as he set five new records as a rookie quarterback in what many consider the most dominant debut season in NFL history. However, of those five records, only one stands to this day, and Manning is just waiting for the day a young quarterback snatches that record from him. Peyton Manning once revealed the real reason he wants his NFL rookie record broken During an appearance on the Kittle Things podcast a few months ago, Peyton Manning jokingly explained to George Kittle why he is ready for his last remaining record from his rookie year – the record for most interceptions thrown by a rookie – to be broken. He noted that coaches don’t allow their rookie quarterbacks to make mistakes and stay in the game, and that is standing in the way of his record possibly being broken. “Am I proud to hold the NFL interception rookie record? No,” Manning said on Kittle’s podcast earlier this year. “Would I like to get it broken? Yes. Do I think it should be with 17 games now? Yes. Do the coaches take the rookies that are struggling out too early? 100%. “Leave them in there. Let them learn. I’m over it, as you can tell. But that would be my rookie mistake. Respect it, but don’t over-respect it where you kind of get yourself out of whack.” For those unaware, Manning currently holds the record for the most interceptions thrown by a rookie quarterback in a single season with 28. In fact, Manning set five records in his rookie year – most interceptions thrown, most attempts, most completed passes, most passing yards, and most passing touchdowns. Out of these records, all except his interceptions record have been broken, with his completed passes and passing touchdowns thrown records being the last to stand till Justin Herbert broke both of them in the 2020 season. While stars on the team like Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby have struggled, one player is on fire. Karl-Anthony Towns was instrumental in helping the Knicks win it all last season. technology.title: The world's fastest computers have a problem: Keeping the work running
technology.description: Frontier, Oak Ridge National Laboratory's exascale supercomputer, has thousands of processors working together on scientific problems. It also has a surprisingly ordinary way of ruining a researcher's day: one node going down. An uncorrectable memory error can do it, or a maintenance mishap. Scott Atchley , chief technology officer at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, describes technicians accidentally rebooting the wrong node or risking a neighboring node's power supply while working in tightly packed racks. The hardware fault can affect just one node, but a simulation running across thousands of processors can grind to a halt. Then comes a series of questions. How recently did the application save its progress? How much computation needs repeating? And how long before the scheduler lets the job run again? For operators, the challenge isn't just keeping the supercomputer running. It's keeping the science moving. One bad node and everybody suffers On Frontier , a memory error can have an outsized audience. Atchley says uncorrectable double-bit errors in high-bandwidth memory occurred about 1.5 times a day during the supercomputer's early bring-up. Its predecessor, Summit, saw roughly one every two weeks. This sounds like a backward step, until you count the memory. Frontier has more than 16 times as much, giving bad bits considerably more places to hide. Memory isn't the only problem. Problematic GPU firmware can crash a node, and so can a technician rebooting the wrong one. Interconnect faults add another way for a large job to come unstuck. In a tightly coupled simulation using the Message Passing Interface (MPI) simulation, thousands of processes, or ranks, exchange data and participate in collective operations. If one rank disappears, the others cannot carry on as though nothing happened. Clockwork.io CEO Suresh Vasudevan describes a similar dependency in synchronized GPU training. One failed GPU can bring a 1,024-GPU job to a pause. An underperforming GPU can be almost as troublesome: if one participant runs at 80 percent speed, others might have to spend time waiting for it. The bigger the machine, the more ways there are for one small problem to become everybody's problem. How often should you hit save? Since stopping every component from failing isn't an option, researchers need a way to preserve their work. That's where checkpointing comes in. The application periodically saves its state so that, when something goes wrong, the simulation can resume from an earlier point instead of starting from scratch. The catch is that saving progress costs computing time, and doing it too often can become almost as wasteful as losing the work itself. Vasudevan explains this with an example. This case kicked off in 2020, when the US Department of Justice claimed entities Huawei operated in America violated federal law. The indictment led to a trial on a dozen criminal matters that has played out over the last three months in the Eastern District Court of New York. The trial ended on Tuesday when a jury found Huawei and three subsidiary companies guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, conspiracy to commit wire and bank fraud, wire fraud, bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the United States, conspiracy to violate the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) and substantive violations of that law, plus money laundering conspiracy. The Department of Justice’s celebration of the decision says Huawei was found to have stolen Cisco’s source code, after prosecutors showed evidence that “Huawei engineers left Cisco’s notes about the Cisco code, referred to Cisco using its name backwards ‘ocsic’ and described that portions of the code remained as they existed in the ‘ocsic’ code.” Another item of evidence apparently showed a Huawei staffer photographing Fujitsu equipment while wearing a fake employee badge for a company called “Weihua” – cunningly reversing the two syllables of “Huawei.” Another allegation the jury accepted involved Huawei staffers signing a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) ahead of a visit to T-Mobile to inspect a robot the telco created to test mobile devices. Huawei staff ignored that NDA so thoroughly that they “sent photographs and technical details of the robot back to China” so the Chinese company could make its own robot. “When that data was not sufficient, a Huawei employee stole a part of the robot in his backpack and carried it out of T-Mobile’s controlled laboratory,” the DoJ says. The feds say the Chinese company also “lied about its activities in Iran to banks to obtain billions of U.S. dollars and access to U.S.-dollar clearing services, which enabled Huawei to be a sophisticated participant in a global marketplace for telecommunications services — in part because of its lies.” Huawei has issued a statement noting that the jury found it not guilty of racketeering and insisting the charges on which it was found guilty are “without legal or factual merit.” “The five trade secret-related disputes cited by the government were all civil matters that were resolved over the past two decades,” the statement adds. Sentencing will take place in September 2027.
